seo.description: 20 High-yield JEE Main MCQ practice questions covering vertical circular motion, critical velocities at lowest/topmost points, string slacking vs oscillation regimes, light rigid rod loop conditions, looping the loop, and aircraft dive pull-outs.

conceptCapsule.title: Dynamics & Energy Conservation in Vertical Circular Motion
conceptCapsule.summary: 1. Flexible String / Track Constraints: To complete a vertical circle of radius $L$, the string must remain taut at the apex ($T_{\text{top}} \ge 0$), requiring $v_{\text{top}} \ge \sqrt{gL}$ and lowest speed $u \ge \sqrt{5gL}$. 2. Kinematic Regimes for a String-Bob System: (a) $0 < u \le \sqrt{2gL}$: Oscillates in the lower hemisphere without slacking (max angle $\le 90^\circ$). (b) $\sqrt{2gL} < u < \sqrt{5gL}$: String slacks ($T = 0$) at an angle $\theta$ to the upward vertical (where $\cos\theta = \frac{u^2 - 2gL}{3gL}$) and executes parabolic projectile motion. (c) $u \ge \sqrt{5gL}$: Completes full vertical circle. 3. Light Rigid Rod / Constrained Bead: Because a rigid rod or wire ring can support compressive forces ($T < 0$ or normal force inwards/outwards), the speed at the top only needs to satisfy $v_{\text{top}} \ge 0$, yielding a minimum bottom speed of $u_{\text{min}} = \sqrt{4gL} = 2\sqrt{gL}$. 4. Tension Difference: For any complete vertical circle under gravity, the difference in string tension between the lowest and highest points is invariant: $T_{\text{bottom}} - T_{\text{top}} = 6mg$.
conceptCapsule.keyFormula: $$u_{\text{min, string}} = \sqrt{5gL}, \quad u_{\text{min, rod}} = \sqrt{4gL}, \quad v_{\text{top, min}} = \sqrt{gL}, \quad T_L - T_H = 6mg, \quad \cos\theta_{\text{slack}} = \frac{u^2 - 2gL}{3gL}$$
conceptCapsule.examTrap: Remember that a light string slacks when $T = 0$ while velocity is still non-zero ($v^2 = gL\cos\theta$), after which the bob becomes a free projectile. In contrast, when $u \le \sqrt{2gL}$, the velocity drops to zero while tension is non-zero ($T = mg\cos\theta$), causing simple oscillation!

questions.statement: A small bob attached to a light inextensible string of length $L$ is whirled in a vertical circle. The minimum speed $u_{\text{min}}$ that must be imparted to the bob at the lowest point to just complete the full vertical circle without the string slacking is:
questions.solution:
Condition to loop the circle: $T_{\text{top}} \ge 0 \implies v_{\text{top, min}} = \sqrt{gL}$.
By conservation of mechanical energy: $\frac{1}{2}m u^2 = \frac{1}{2}m v_{\text{top}}^2 + mg(2L) \implies u^2 = gL + 4gL = 5gL \implies u_{\text{min}} = \sqrt{5gL}$.
Therefore, Option B is correct.

questions.statement: In Question 1, when the bob is projected with the minimum velocity to complete the loop ($u = \sqrt{5gL}$), the speed of the bob at the topmost point is:
questions.solution:
$$v_{\text{top}} = \sqrt{u^2 - 4gL} = \sqrt{5gL - 4gL} = \sqrt{gL}$$
Therefore, Option A is correct.

questions.statement: A small sphere of mass $m$ tied to a string of length $L$ is projected with speed $u = \sqrt{5gL}$ at the lowest point. The difference between the tension in the string at the lowest point ($T_L$) and at the highest point ($T_H$) is:
questions.solution:
At bottom: $T_L = \frac{m(5gL)}{L} + mg = 6mg$.
At top: $T_H = \frac{m(gL)}{L} - mg = 0$.
Difference: $T_L - T_H = 6mg - 0 = 6mg$. (In general, for any complete vertical circle, $T_L - T_H = 6mg$ always holds).
Therefore, Option C is correct.

questions.statement: A small ball of mass $m$ is attached to the end of a light rigid rod of length $L$ pivoted at the center. The minimum horizontal speed $u$ that must be imparted to the ball at the lowest point so that it completes a full vertical circle is:
questions.solution:
A rigid rod can support compressive thrust, so speed at the top only needs to satisfy $v_{\text{top}} \ge 0$.
$$\frac{1}{2}m u^2 = mg(2L) \implies u_{\text{min}} = \sqrt{4gL} = 2\sqrt{gL}$$
Therefore, Option B is correct.

questions.statement: A body of mass $m$ tied to a string of length $L$ is projected at the lowest point with horizontal speed $u = \sqrt{2gL}$. The motion of the body will be:

options.text: Simple oscillation in the lower half with maximum angular amplitude $90^\circ$
Leaving the circular path between $\theta = 90^\circ$ and $180^\circ$ and following a parabolic trajectory
Coming to rest permanently at the lowest point

questions.solution:
When $u = \sqrt{2gL}$, maximum height reached is $h = \frac{u^2}{2g} = L$, which corresponds to the horizontal position ($\theta = 90^\circ$). Velocity vanishes before tension can drop to zero, so the bob undergoes simple oscillation in the lower hemisphere.
Therefore, Option B is correct.

questions.statement: A stone of mass $m$ is tied to a string of length $L$ and projected horizontally at the lowest point with speed $u = \sqrt{4gL}$. The height $h$ above the lowest point at which the string becomes slack is:
questions.solution:
Let string slack at angle $\alpha$ with upward vertical: $T = 0 \implies v^2 = gL\cos\alpha$.
By energy conservation: $4gL = gL\cos\alpha + 2gL(1 + \cos\alpha) \implies 3\cos\alpha = 2 \implies \cos\alpha = \frac{2}{3}$.
Height above bottom: $h = L(1 + \cos\alpha) = L\left(1 + \frac{2}{3}\right) = \frac{5}{3}L$.
Therefore, Option B is correct.

questions.statement: In Question 6, after the string becomes slack, the subsequent motion of the stone until the string tightens again is:

options.text: Uniform circular motion of smaller radius

questions.solution:
Once the string slacks ($T = 0$), the stone moves freely under gravity with an initial velocity directed obliquely upward, tracing a parabolic projectile trajectory.
Therefore, Option B is correct.

questions.statement: A block of mass $m$ is released from rest at height $h$ on a smooth track that leads into a vertical circular loop of radius $R$. If the block is to maintain continuous contact with the track throughout the loop, the minimum height $h$ is:
questions.solution:
$$mgh = \frac{1}{2}m v_{\text{bottom}}^2 = \frac{1}{2}m(5gR) \implies h = 2.5 R$$
Therefore, Option C is correct.

questions.statement: A motorcyclist loops the loop inside a spherical cage of radius $R = 10\text{ m}$. The minimum speed required at the top of the loop so that the tyres remain in contact with the cage is ($g = 10\text{ m/s}^2$):
questions.solution:
$$v_{\text{top, min}} = \sqrt{gR} = \sqrt{10 \times 10} = 10.0\text{ m/s}$$
Therefore, Option A is correct.

questions.statement: A bucket filled with water is rotated in a vertical circle of radius $R = 2.5\text{ m}$. The minimum angular velocity $\omega_{\text{min}}$ at the top of the circle so that water does not spill out is ($g = 10\text{ m/s}^2$):
questions.solution:
$$\omega_{\text{min}} = \sqrt{\frac{g}{R}} = \sqrt{\frac{10}{2.5}} = \sqrt{4} = 2\text{ rad/s}$$
Therefore, Option C is correct.

questions.statement: A particle of mass $m$ is attached to a string of length $L$ and whirled in a vertical circle. If the ratio of maximum to minimum tension in the string is $4 : 1$, the speed of the particle at the lowest point is:
questions.solution:
1. $T_{\text{max}} = \frac{mu^2}{L} + mg$, $T_{\text{min}} = \frac{m(u^2 - 4gL)}{L} - mg = \frac{mu^2}{L} - 5mg$.
2. $\frac{u^2/L + g}{u^2/L - 5g} = 4 \implies u^2/L + g = 4u^2/L - 20g \implies 3u^2/L = 21g \implies u = \sqrt{7gL}$.
Therefore, Option B is correct.

questions.statement: A bead of mass $m$ is free to slide on a smooth vertical circular wire loop of radius $R$. The minimum speed $u$ given to the bead at the lowest point so that it reaches the top of the loop is:
questions.solution:
The wire loop constrains the bead on both sides, so speed at top only needs $v_{\text{top}} \ge 0$:
$$\frac{1}{2}m u^2 = mg(2R) \implies u_{\text{min}} = \sqrt{4gR}$$
Therefore, Option B is correct.

questions.statement: A particle of mass $m$ suspended from a string of length $L$ is projected horizontally from the lowest point with speed $u = \sqrt{7gL}$. The tension in the string when it becomes horizontal is:
questions.solution:
1. Speed at horizontal: $v^2 = u^2 - 2gL = 7gL - 2gL = 5gL$.
2. Tension: $T = \frac{mv^2}{L} = \frac{m(5gL)}{L} = 5mg$.
Therefore, Option B is correct.

questions.statement: A string of length $L$ carrying a bob of mass $m$ is deflected by $90^\circ$ from the vertical so that it is horizontal, and then released from rest. The tension in the string when the bob passes through the lowest point is:
questions.solution:
1. Speed at bottom: $\frac{1}{2}mv^2 = mgL \implies v^2 = 2gL$.
2. Tension: $T = mg + \frac{mv^2}{L} = mg + 2mg = 3mg$.
Therefore, Option C is correct.

questions.statement: A pendulum bob of mass $m$ is suspended by a string of length $L$. It is given a speed $u$ at the bottom such that the string slacks at an angle $\phi = 120^\circ$ from the bottom upward. The speed $u$ is:
questions.solution:
Angle with upward vertical is $\alpha = 180^\circ - 120^\circ = 60^\circ$.
At slacking: $v^2 = gL\cos 60^\circ = 0.5gL$.
Energy conservation: $u^2 = v^2 + 2gL(1 + \cos 60^\circ) = 0.5gL + 3gL = 3.5gL \implies u = \sqrt{3.5gL}$.
Therefore, Option A is correct.

questions.statement: A small body of mass $m$ is placed on top of a smooth sphere of radius $R$. When slightly disturbed, it slides down. The angle $	heta$ with the vertical at which the body breaks away from the surface is:
questions.solution:
$$N = mg(3\cos\theta - 2) = 0 \implies \cos\theta = \frac{2}{3} \implies \theta = \cos^{-1}\left(\frac{2}{3}\right)$$
Therefore, Option A is correct.

questions.statement: An aircraft is pulling out of a vertical dive along a circular arc of radius $R = 400\text{ m}$ at a constant speed of $v = 200\text{ m/s}$. The apparent weight of a pilot of mass $M = 70\text{ kg}$ at the lowest point of the pull-out is ($g = 10\text{ m/s}^2$):
questions.solution:
$$N = M\left(g + \frac{v^2}{R} ight) = 70\left(10 + \frac{200^2}{400} ight) = 70(10 + 100) = 7700\text{ N}$$
Therefore, Option C is correct.

questions.statement: A body moves in a vertical circle of radius $R$ attached to a string. At any position where the string makes an angle $	heta$ with the downward vertical, the tension $T$ is related to speed $v$ by:
questions.solution:
$$T - mg\cos\theta = \frac{mv^2}{R} \implies T = \frac{mv^2}{R} + mg\cos\theta$$
Therefore, Option A is correct.

questions.statement: A mass $m$ tied to a string of length $L$ is rotated in a vertical circle. If the total energy of the system is $E = \dfrac{5}{2}mgL$ taking potential energy zero at the lowest point, the tension at the highest point of the loop is:
questions.solution:
1. At top: $U = 2mgL \implies K = E - U = \frac{5}{2}mgL - 2mgL = \frac{1}{2}mgL \implies v_{\text{top}}^2 = gL$.
2. Tension: $T_{\text{top}} = \frac{mv_{\text{top}}^2}{L} - mg = mg - mg = 0$.
Therefore, Option A is correct.

questions.statement: A heavy ball is suspended by a light string of length $L$. The string is given an initial horizontal velocity $u = \sqrt{6gL}$ at the lowest point. The ratio of the maximum tension to the minimum tension in the loop is:
questions.solution:
1. Bottom tension: $T_L = \frac{m(6gL)}{L} + mg = 7mg$.
2. Top speed: $v_H^2 = 6gL - 4gL = 2gL \implies T_H = \frac{m(2gL)}{L} - mg = mg$.
3. Ratio: $\frac{T_L}{T_H} = \frac{7mg}{mg} = 7 : 1$.
Therefore, Option A is correct.
